title: Kernel Representation and Similarity Measure for Incomplete Data
Kernel Representation and Similarity Measure for Incomplete Data
summary: The paper addresses similarity measurement between incomplete data samples, where traditional deletion or imputation-based approaches lose information or introduce bias. It proposes the proximity kernel, which combines equal-frequency binning, proximity (Voronoi) assignment, one-hot encoding, and a three-level cascading fallback strategy using kernel mean embedding for missing features. Experiments on 12 UCI incomplete datasets show the proposed method achieves the highest average NMI of 0.4245, best or second-best NMI on 10 of 12 datasets, and linear time complexity in the number of samples.

approach: Reimplement the proximity kernel from the paper for the target claim C1 on the UCI Hepatitis dataset. For each feature, equal-frequency binning uses evenly-spaced percentiles of observed values only, then each observed value is assigned to its nearest bin center and encoded as a one-hot vector. Missing feature encodings are filled by a three-level cascading fallback (intersection matching, union matching, global prior) using kernel mean embedding over matching samples. The resulting representation Z is clustered with sklearn KMeans using the ground-truth number of clusters, NMI is averaged over 10 random seeds, and nbins is searched over {2,3,4,6,8} by mean NMI. Finally, reproduce.py writes results/metrics.json comparing the selected NMI to the target 0.2289 within ±0.02.
steps: Setup: confirm numpy, pandas, scikit-learn are installed. No extra packages are required because pandas can read the UCI URL directly. Set all random seeds via the seed lists in config.

Implement src/data.py: read https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/hepatitis/hepatitis.data with pandas.read_csv(header=None, na_values=['?', '']); X = df.iloc[:, 1:].astype(float).values; y = df.iloc[:, 0].astype(int).values - 1; assert X.shape == (155, 19), y.shape == (155,), len(np.unique(y)) == 2; return X, y, K=2.

Implement src/proximity_kernel.py fit_bins(X, nbins): for each feature j, obs = X[~np.isnan(X[:, j]), j]; if len(obs) == 0, centers = None and prior = uniform 1/nbins; else centers = np.percentile(obs, 100*np.arange(1, nbins+1)/(nbins+1), method='linear'); store centers and global prior frequencies.

Implement proximity_kernel.py assign_bins(X, centers): for each observed value, k = np.argmin(np.abs(x - centers)); tie breaks to lowest index; store integer bin assignments B (n, d) with -1 for missing entries.
Implement proximity_kernel.py encode_observed(B, nbins): build H_obs (n, d, nbins) with H_obs[i, j, B[i, j]] = 1 for observed entries, zeros for missing entries.

Implement proximity_kernel.py compute_fallback_encodings(X, B, H_obs, centers, nbins): for each missing entry (i, j), let O_i = observed features of i and B_i = B[i, O_i]. Level 1: S1 = {m != i : X[m, l] observed and B[m, l] == B[i, l] for all l in O_i}; S1_j = {m in S1 : X[m, j] observed}; if S1_j nonempty, h = mean(H_obs[m, j] for m in S1_j). Level 2: if S1_j empty, S2 = union_{l in O_i} {m != i : X[m, l] observed and B[m, l] == B[i, l]}; S2_j = {m in S2 : X[m, j] observed}; if S2_j nonempty, h = mean(H_obs[m, j] for m in S2_j). Level 3: if S2_j empty, h = global prior for feature j (bin frequencies among observed values, or uniform 1/nbins if feature entirely missing). Store H[i, j] = h and record level counts.

Implement proximity_kernel.py build_representation(X, nbins): call fit_bins, assign_bins, encode_observed, compute_fallback_encodings; concatenate H[i, j] across j to get Z (n, d*nbins); return Z and diagnostics including missing entry count and level 1/2/3 counts.
Implement proximity_kernel.py proximity_kernel(Z): return K = Z @ Z.T / d where d = 19; use only for symmetry and bounds checks.

Implement src/cluster.py evaluate_nbins(Z, y, K, seeds): for each seed, run KMeans(n_clusters=K, init='k-means++', n_init=10, random_state=seed).fit(Z); labels = kmeans.labels_; nmi = normalized_mutual_info_score(y, labels); return mean, std, per-seed list.

Implement src/cluster.py search_nbins(X, y, K, nbins_grid, seeds): for each nbins in nbins_grid, call build_representation, evaluate_nbins, and record mean/std/per-seed; select best nbins as the one with highest mean NMI; return best_nbins, best_mean, all_results.

Implement reproduce.py: parse optional --smoke flag. If smoke, load data, subset first 20 rows, run build_representation with nbins=2, assert Z.shape == (20, 38), assert no NaN/inf, assert each observed-feature one-hot sums to 1 and each missing-feature fallback vector sums to 1, compute K and assert symmetry and diagonal <= 1, run one KMeans with seed 0, print NMI and diagnostics. Otherwise run search_nbins on full Hepatitis with nbins_grid and seeds.
Run smoke test: python reproduce.py --smoke. Verify output shows correct shapes, no NaNs, at least one missing entry resolved by level 1 or 2, and a valid NMI in [0, 1].

Run intermediate checks before full run: print X shape (155, 19), y shape (155,), class counts, total missing entries and per-feature missing counts; verify bin centers are strictly increasing for features with observed values; verify B indices are in [0, nbins-1]; verify H row sums per feature are 1 for all samples; print fallback level counts (level 3 should be rare, <5% of missing entries); verify K is symmetric, K_ii <= 1, K_ij in [0, 1]; run a sanity baseline KMeans on median-imputed raw features and record its NMI for reference.
Run full reproduction: python reproduce.py. This runs 5 nbins values × 10 seeds = 50 KMeans runs on 155 samples; each run is seconds or less.

Inspect results/metrics.json: check the C1 value, best_nbins, per-nbins means, and per-seed NMI spread. Compare |value - 0.2289| <= 0.02. If outside tolerance, run sensitivity variants: (a) percentile centers at 100*(k-0.5)/nbins; (b) percentile centers at 100*k/nbins; (c) kernel K-means assigning each point to the cluster maximizing average K to cluster members. Record each variant's value and choose the most faithful documented variant; otherwise keep the primary result.
Finalize results/metrics.json with the chosen C1 value, target 0.2289, tolerance 0.02, pass/fail boolean, best nbins, per-nbins and per-seed results, diagnostics, runtime, and environment metadata.
smoke_test: python reproduce.py --smoke: loads Hepatitis, subsets first 20 rows, builds Z with nbins=2, checks Z shape == (20, 38), no NaN/inf, each feature encoding sums to 1 per sample, kernel K = Z @ Z.T / 19 is symmetric with diagonal <= 1, at least one missing entry resolved by level 1 or 2, runs KMeans(n_clusters=2, init='k-means++', n_init=10, random_state=0), and prints an NMI in [0, 1].
intermediate_checks: Dataset size: X.shape == (155, 19), y.shape == (155,), number of classes == 2.
Class balance: print counts of y == 0 and y == 1 (expected approximately 32/123 for Hepatitis; exact counts are fine).
Missingness: total number of NaN entries and per-feature NaN counts; confirm common UCI missing markers '?' were converted to NaN.
Binning: for each feature with observed values, the nbins bin centers are strictly increasing; for any entirely missing feature, uniform prior is used.
Proximity assignment: all non-missing bin indices B[i, j] are in [0, nbins-1]; missing entries are -1.
One-hot encoding: for every sample and every feature, the encoding vector h_{i,j} sums to 1 (exactly 1 for observed, probabilities summing to 1 for missing).
Fallback diagnostics: count missing entries resolved by level 1, level 2, and level 3; level 3 should be rare (<5% of missing entries).
Kernel matrix: K = Z @ Z.T / 19 is symmetric, K_ii <= 1, and all entries are in [0, 1].
Sanity baseline: KMeans on raw features with median imputation gives some NMI; record it to ensure the proximity kernel result is not identical to a trivial imputation baseline.
Parameter count: Z has shape (155, 19*nbins); for nbins in {2,3,4,6,8} this is 38, 57, 76, 114, 152 features.

import os

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

DATA_URL = "https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/hepatitis/hepatitis.data"
CACHE_NAME = "hepatitis.data"
MISSING_MARKERS = ["?", "", " ", "NA", "NaN", "nan"]


def _cache_dir():
    d = os.environ.get("REPRO_DATA_CACHE")
    if d:

        return d
    return os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))), "data_cache")


def _download():
    """Download hepatitis.data into the shared cache (only if not present)."""
    cache_dir = _cache_dir()
    path = os.path.join(cache_dir, CACHE_NAME)
    if os.path.exists(path) and os.path.getsize(path) > 0:
        return path
    import urllib.request

    os.makedirs(cache_dir, exist_ok=True)
    urllib.request.urlretrieve(DATA_URL, path)
    return path

"""Proximity kernel for incomplete data (reimplementation from the paper).

Paper: "Kernel Representation and Similarity Measure for Incomplete Data"
(Cao et al., arXiv:2510.13352), Section 4.

Components
----------
1. Equal-frequency binning (Sec. 4.1.1, Eq. 4): for each feature j the nbins
   bin centers are evenly-spaced percentiles of the *observed* values only,
   c_{j,k} = percentile(X_obs,j, (k-1) * 100 / (nbins - 1)), k = 1..nbins.
   Hence c_{j,1} = min and c_{j,nbins} = max of the observed values.
2. Proximity assignment (Sec. 4.1.2, Eq. 5): each observed value is assigned to
   its nearest bin center (Voronoi cell); ties go to the lowest bin index.
3. One-hot encoding (Sec. 4.1.3, Eqs. 6-7): h_{i,j} is a one-hot vector of
   length nbins; z_i concatenates the h_{i,j} over all d features.
4. Cascading fallback for missing entries (Sec. 4.2):
   Level 1 (Eqs. 8-10): S1(i) = intersection over observed features j of the
     samples m != i sharing sample i's bin in feature j; the missing encoding
     is the kernel mean embedding (mean one-hot) over S1(i).
   Level 2 (Eqs. 11-12): S2(i) = union of those per-feature match sets; mean
     one-hot over S2(i).
   Level 3 (Eqs. 13-14): global prior p_{j,k} = fraction of observed values of
     feature j falling in bin k.
5. Proximity kernel (Sec. 4.3, Eq. 15): K(x_m, x_n) = (1/d) z_m^T z_n.
"""

import numpy as np


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# 1. Equal-frequency binning
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def fit_bins(X, nbins):
    """Compute bin centers and global priors for every feature.

    Returns
    -------
    centers : list of length d; entry j is an array of nbins centers or None
        when feature j has no observed values at all.
    priors  : (d, nbins) array of global bin priors (rows sum to 1).
    """
    n, d = X.shape
    centers = []
    priors = np.zeros((d, nbins), dtype=float)
    for j in range(d):
        obs = X[~np.isnan(X[:, j]), j]
        if obs.size == 0:
            centers.append(None)
            priors[j] = 1.0 / nbins
            continue
        # Eq. (4): evenly-spaced percentiles, endpoints are min and max.
        pcts = np.arange(nbins) * (100.0 / (nbins - 1))
        c = np.percentile(obs, pcts, method="linear")
        centers.append(c)
        counts = np.bincount(assign_bins(obs, c), minlength=nbins).astype(float)
        priors[j] = counts / counts.sum()
    return centers, priors


def assign_bins(values, centers):
    """Proximity assignment: nearest bin center (Eq. 5); ties -> lowest index."""
    values = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
    centers = np.asarray(centers, dtype=float)
    dist = np.abs(values[:, None] - centers[None, :])
    return np.argmin(dist, axis=1).astype(int)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# 2. One-hot encoding of observed values
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def encode_observed(B, nbins):
    """H[i, j, :] is the one-hot encoding of the observed bin of (i, j).

    Missing entries (B == -1) stay all-zero here and are filled later by the
    cascading fallback strategy.
    """
    n, d = B.shape
    H = np.zeros((n, d, nbins), dtype=float)
    rows, cols = np.nonzero(B >= 0)
    H[rows, cols, B[rows, cols]] = 1.0
    return H


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# 3. Cascading fallback strategy
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def _match_sets(B, i, obs_idx):
    """Per-feature match sets C_{i,j} = {m != i : b_{m,j} == b_{i,j}}."""
    sets = []
    for j in obs_idx:
        b = B[i, j]
        m = np.nonzero((B[:, j] == b))[0]
        m = m[m != i]
        sets.append(set(m.tolist()))
    return sets


def fill_missing(X, B, H, centers, priors, nbins, kme_observed_only=True):
    """Fill the encodings of missing entries with the 3-level cascade.

    Parameters
    ----------
    kme_observed_only : bool
        The paper's Eqs. (10)/(12) average h_{m,j} over the matching set
        S1(i)/S2(i).  h_{m,j} is only defined for samples m whose feature j is
        observed, so by default the mean is taken over the matching samples
        that actually have feature j observed.  When False, the mean is taken
        over *all* matching samples using their (already filled) encodings,
        which is the literal reading of the equations.
    """
    n, d = X.shape
    observed = ~np.isnan(X)
    levels = np.zeros((n, d), dtype=int)  # 0 = observed, 1/2/3 = fallback level
    for i in range(n):
        obs_idx = np.nonzero(observed[i])[0]
        mis_idx = np.nonzero(~observed[i])[0]
        if mis_idx.size == 0:
            continue
        if obs_idx.size == 0:
            # No observed feature at all: nothing to match on -> global prior.
            for j in mis_idx:
                H[i, j] = priors[j]
                levels[i, j] = 3
            continue
        per_feature = _match_sets(B, i, obs_idx)
        s1 = set.intersection(*per_feature) if per_feature else set()
        s2 = set.union(*per_feature) if per_feature else set()
        for j in mis_idx:
            if s1:
                cand = [m for m in s1 if observed[m, j]] if kme_observed_only else list(s1)
                if cand:
                    H[i, j] = H[cand, j, :].mean(axis=0)
                    levels[i, j] = 1
                    continue
            if s2:
                cand = [m for m in s2 if observed[m, j]] if kme_observed_only else list(s2)
                if cand:
                    H[i, j] = H[cand, j, :].mean(axis=0)
                    levels[i, j] = 2
                    continue
            H[i, j] = priors[j]
            levels[i, j] = 3
    return H, levels


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# 4. Full representation + kernel
# ---------------

"""Clustering evaluation of the proximity-kernel representation (Sec. 5.1).

Protocol from the paper:
  * K-means with the number of clusters equal to the ground-truth number of
    classes, applied to the representation z_i (Sec. 4.4, Eq. 19).
  * NMI (Normalized Mutual Information) as the clustering metric.
  * Each experiment is run 10 times and the results are averaged.
  * nbins is searched over {2, 3, 4, 6, 8}.
"""

import numpy as np
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
from sklearn.metrics import normalized_mutual_info_score

from src.proximity_kernel import build_representation

NBINS_GRID = [2, 3, 4, 6, 8]
SEEDS = list(range(10))
KMEANS_N_INIT = 10


def evaluate_representation(Z, y, n_clusters, seeds=SEEDS, n_init=KMEANS_N_INIT):
    """Run K-means on Z for every seed; return per-seed NMI plus mean/std."""
    nmis = []
    for seed in seeds:
        km = KMeans(n_clusters=n_clusters, init="k-means++", n_init=n_init,
                    random_state=seed)
        labels = km.fit_predict(Z)
        nmis.append(float(normalized_mutual_info_score(y, labels)))
    nmis = np.asarray(nmis, dtype=float)
    return {"per_seed": nmis.tolist(), "mean": float(nmis.mean()),
            "std": float(nmis.std(ddof=0))}


def search_nbins(X, y, n_clusters, nbins_grid=NBINS_GRID, seeds=SEEDS,
                 kme_observed_only=True, verbose=True):
    """Search nbins; the reported value is the best mean NMI over the grid."""
    results = {}
    for nbins in nbins_grid:
        Z, diag = build_representation(X, nbins, kme_observed_only=kme_observed_only)
        res = evaluate_representation(Z, y, n_clusters, seeds=seeds)
        res["diagnostics"] = diag
        results[nbins] = res
        if verbose:
            print(f"  nbins={nbins}: mean NMI={res['mean']:.4f} "
                  f"(std {res['std']:.4f}) levels={diag['level_counts']}")
    best_nbins = max(results, key=lambda k: results[k]["mean"])
    return best_nbins, results

"""Sensitivity analysis for the C1 (Hepatitis) result.

Checks how the reported NMI depends on implementation choices that the paper
does not pin down exactly:
  * KME averaging over matching samples with feature j observed (primary) vs.
    over all matching samples (literal reading of Eqs. 10/12).
  * Bin centers at percentiles (k-1)*100/(nbins-1) (paper Eq. 4, primary) vs.
    k*100/(nbins+1) (an alternative "evenly spaced percentile" convention).
  * Tie-breaking in the nearest-center assignment.
"""

import numpy as np

from src.cluster import NBINS_GRID, SEEDS, evaluate_representation
from src.data import load_hepatitis
from src.proximity_kernel import build_representation, fit_bins, assign_bins


def variant_centers(X, nbins, mode):
    """Rebuild the representation with an alternative bin-center convention."""
    from src.proximity_kernel import encode_observed, fill_missing
    n, d = X.shape
    centers, priors = [], np.zeros((d, nbins))
    for j in range(d):
        obs = X[~np.isnan(X[:, j]), j]
        if obs.size == 0:
            centers.append(None)
            priors[j] = 1.0 / nbins
            continue
        if mode == "paper":          # Eq. (4): endpoints are min and max
            pcts = np.arange(nbins) * (100.0 / (nbins - 1))
        elif mode == "midpoint":     # k*100/(nbins+1)
            pcts = (np.arange(nbins) + 1) * (100.0 / (nbins + 1))
        elif mode == "edges":        # k*100/nbins
            pcts = (np.arange(nbins) + 1) * (100.0 / nbins)
        c = np.percentile(obs, pcts, method="linear")
        centers.append(c)
        counts = np.bincount(assign_bins(obs, c), minlength=nbins).astype(float)
        priors[j] = counts / counts.sum()
    B = np.full((n, d), -1, dtype=int)
    for j in range(d):
        if centers[j] is None:
            continue
        rows = np.nonzero(~np.isnan(X[:, j]))[0]
        B[rows, j] = assign_bins(X[rows, j], centers[j])
    H = encode_observed(B, nbins)
    H, _ = fill_missing(X, B, H, centers, priors, nbins)
    return H.reshape(n, d * nbins)


def main():
    X, y, K = load_hepatitis()
    print("primary (KME over matching samples with feature j observed):")
    for nb in NBINS_GRID:
        Z, _ = build_representation(X, nb)
        r = evaluate_representation(Z, y, K)
        print(f"  nbins={nb}: {r['mean']:.4f}")

    print("literal KME (mean over all matching samples, incl. missing j):")
    for nb in NBINS_GRID:
        Z, _ = build_representation(X, nb, kme_observed_only=False)
        r = evaluate_representation(Z, y, K)
        print(f"  nbins={nb}: {r['mean']:.4f}")

    for mode in ("midpoint", "edges"):
        print(f"bin centers = {mode} percentiles:")
        for nb in NBINS_GRID:
            Z = variant_centers(X, nb, mode)
            r = evaluate_representation(Z, y, K)
            print(f"  nbins={nb}: {r['mean']:.4f}")

    # exact value at the selected configuration
    Z, _ = build_representation(X, 2)
    r = evaluate_representation(Z, y, K)
    print("exact NMI at nbins=2 (primary):", repr(r["per_seed"][0]))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

target.statement: Proximity kernel ('Ours') achieves NMI 0.2289 on the Hepatitis dataset under K-means clustering with the ground-truth number of clusters.
target.dataset: Hepatitis (UCI; 155 samples, 19 features, 2 classes per Table 2)

tolerance.why: Rule 3: NMI is a bounded [0,1] score on the Hepatitis dataset (155 examples, smaller than 2,000) and the paper prints values as fractions, so the band is 0.02 absolute.

audit_summary: The clean rerun computes C1 on the full UCI Hepatitis dataset (155x19, 2 classes, 167 missing entries) with the proximity-kernel pipeline and K-means at the ground-truth K=2, averaging 10 seeds. The reported 0.2289 is computed from the representation, not assigned from the target constant; the matching literal in reproduce.py is only TARGET_VALUE for pass/fail. The nbins grid {2,3,4,6,8} was searched and nbins=2 gives 0.2289, while alternative binning conventions give different values, supporting the chosen Eq. (4) interpretation. Fidelity is good for R1-R4 and R6-R12/R14, with disclosed reader assumptions A1/A11 (ordinal categorical coding, no scaling) and A14 (observed-only KME). The only requirement not fully evidenced is R13: the code has no complexity test and its fallback loop is quadratic in n, though this does not affect the C1 value. C2-C8 were not reproduced; the extra peek_cache.py activity is unrelated scope creep.

requirement_check.evidence: fit_bins() computes centers per feature from obs = X[~isnan(X[:,j]), j] only; missing entries never enter percentile or prior estimation.
pcts = arange(nbins)*100/(nbins-1); np.percentile(obs, pcts, method='linear'), so endpoints are min/max and centers are evenly-spaced percentiles.
assign_bins() uses argmin(|value-center|); np.argmin tie-breaks to the lowest bin index.
encode_observed() writes one-hot H[i,j,:]; Z = H.reshape(n, d*nbins).
_match_sets() builds per-observed-feature same-bin sets; s1 = intersection; for missing j, H[i,j] = mean H[cand,j,:] over s1 samples observing j (A14).
When no level-1 candidate exists, s2 = union of per-feature match sets is used and mean one-hot over observed candidates is assigned.
If no level-2 candidate exists, H[i,j] = priors[j]; priors are observed bin frequencies, uniform for an entirely missing feature.
kernel_from_representation() computes K = Z Z^T / d. The primary evaluation clusters Z; for this linear kernel that is equivalent to kernel K-means on K.
evaluate_representation() runs sklearn KMeans(n_clusters=K=2, init='k-means++', n_init=10) and scores with normalized_mutual_info_score; K is the ground-truth class count.
SEEDS=range(10); metrics.json contains 10 per-seed NMIs and their mean for each nbins.
NBINS_GRID=[2,3,4,6,8]; search_nbins() evaluates all five; best_nbins=2 selected by mean NMI.

No scaling/timing test was run. Binning/assignment are near O(d n log n + nd), but fill_missing scans all n samples for each observed feature of each sample (O(n^2 d)), so the implementation as written is not the paper's stated linear O(nd + d n log n).
For complete data fill_missing leaves H unchanged, and encode_observed() writes exactly one 1 per feature; hence Z has exactly d ones out of d*nbins.
